{{nihongo|'''Shitori Shrine'''|倭文神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} in the Miyauchi neighborhood of the town of {{ill|Yurihama, Tottori|lt=Yurihama|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yurihama, Tottori|qq=}} in {{ill|Tottori Prefecture|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tottori Prefecture|qq=}}, {{ill|Japan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan|qq=}}, on the east bank of {{ill|Lake Tōgō|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lake Tōgō|qq=}}. It is the ''{{ill|ichinomiya|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/ichinomiya|qq=}}'' of former {{ill|Hōki Province|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hōki Province|qq=}}. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on 1 May.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese|qq=draft}}</ref>

==History==
The origins of Shitori Shrine are unknown. Although there is no documentary evidence, it is believed that it began as the family shrine for the {{Nihongo|Shitori clan|倭文氏}} of {{ill|Kofun period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} craftsmen who weavers, who regarded {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} as their ancestor. However, the shrine's legends are all centered around {{ill|Shitateruhime|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|ja|下照比売|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q11307233}}, whom the shrine legend claims arrived in this location from {{ill|Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo Taisha|lt=Izumo|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Taisha|qq=}} by boat. She established her residence on the mountain behind this shrine, and after her death, she was buried in a ''{{ill|kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|qq=}}'' constructed in the shrine's precincts.<ref name="Yoshiki">{{cite book|last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese|qq=draft}}</ref>    
The earliest this shrine appears in documentary records is in the AD 808 medical text {{Nihongo|''Daido-ruishu-ho''|大同類聚方|}}. During the {{ill|Sengoku period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}}, the shine was laid to waste, but it was reconstructed by the {{ill|Amago clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amago clan|qq=}} and was later supported by the {{ill|Ikeda clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda clan|qq=}}, the {{ill|Daimyo|daimyō|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimyo|qq=}} of {{ill|Tottori Domain|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tottori Domain|qq=}}. During the {{ill|Meiji period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}} era of {{ill|State Shinto|en|State Shinto|qid=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto}}, the shrine was rated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Shosha|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.<ref>Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125.</ref>
=== Hōki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound===
Until the early 20th century, Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto was regarded as the primary deity of this shrine. However, in 1915 an {{ill|archaeological excavation|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/archaeological excavation|qq=}} discovered that the purported {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=''empun''-style circular Kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}} was actually a {{ill|sutra mound|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sutra mound|qq=}}. The mound had a diameter of 16-meters and height of 1.6 meters. It contains a rectangular stone box that was 1.2 x 0.9 x 0.5 meters made of {{ill|andesite|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/andesite|qq=}} flat stones. The inside was covered with coarse sand, and contained copper sutra cylinder with inscriptions. The inscription was dated 1103 and was inscribed by monk named Kyoson of the Hōki Ichinomiya. In addition to the sutra cylinder, the box contained a gilt-bronze statue of {{ill|Kannon|lt=Kannon|lt=Guanyin|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Guanyin|qq=}}, an image of {{ill|Maitreya|Miroku Bosatsu|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maitreya|qq=}} engraving on a copper plate, a bronze mirror, a cypress fan, a short sword, beads, and copper coins. The sutra mounds are valuable in considering the burial memorial service in the Heian period. The sutra mound was designated as a {{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monuments of Japan|qq=}} in 1935.<ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2116|title= 伯耆一宮経塚|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=January 2, 2023|qq=draft}}</ref> All excavated items are stored at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokyo National Museum|qq=}}.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book|last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403|qq=draft}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
==location==
The shrine is located a 35-minute walk from {{ill|Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|lt=Matsuzaki Station|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|qq=}} on the {{ill|JR West|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR West|qq=}} {{ill|San'in Main Line|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'in Main Line|qq=}}.<ref name="Okada">{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}}</ref>
